instruction: Write count_vowels(text: str) -> int. Count occurrences of the Latin vowels a, e, i, o, and u, including accented forms such as é and ü, without regard to case. A vowel written as a base letter followed by a combining accent counts once. Do not count ligatures such as æ, or y. The input is always a string; return 0 for an empty string. Python standard-library imports are allowed, but third-party dependencies are not.

Write unique_in_order(items: list[int]) -> list[int]. Return each distinct integer exactly once, in the order it first appears in items. Do not modify items. The input is always a list of integers. For an empty list, return an empty list.

signature: merge_integer_maps(left: dict[str, int], right: dict[str, int]) -> dict[str, int]
instruction: Write merge_integer_maps(left: dict[str, int], right: dict[str, int]) -> dict[str, int]. Return a dictionary containing every key from either input. If a key appears in both, its result is the sum of the two integer values. If it appears in only one, preserve that value. Keep keys whose result is zero. Do not modify either input dictionary. The inputs are always dictionaries with string keys and integer values.
